narrative.overview:
NEXflow is a professional tool, not a product experience. The people using it are weighing fish, printing invoices, and reconciling stock at 5 AM. Every design decision is governed by one question: does this make the work faster and more accurate, or does it slow the worker down? Decoration that cannot answer yes is prohibited.

The visual system is Thai-first and task-first. Sarabun handles Thai and Latin with equal precision; the scale stays compact because the UI is dense with data, not sparse with breathing room. The palette is functional — each color carries a status role (action, success, warning, danger, online) and is never used decoratively. The warm paper canvas grounds the interface without pulling attention away from the content. Surfaces separate from each other by tone, not shadow.

The system explicitly rejects: legacy ERP clutter, generic SaaS blue, budget POS aesthetics, and consumer app energy.
keyCharacteristics: Single Thai-optimized typeface at fixed scale — no display/body pairing, no fluid sizes
Five semantic colors, each with a tinted background pair — used for status, never decoration
Flat + tonal surface separation — depth conveyed by background tone, not shadow
Dark violet-black (#241d3d) table headers for authoritative data presentation
Brand gradient (blue→violet) reserved for identity moments only
Compact density: 4px base grid, 15px body, Thai line-height 1.6

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Action Indigo (#3b5bdb) appears only on interactive controls and current selection indicators. It is never used as a decorative accent. Its scarcity makes it trustworthy.

rules.name: The Role Discipline Rule
rules.body: Success Teal signals stock-in and positive financial events. Warning Amber signals low stock and caution. Danger Red signals void, cancellation, and out-of-stock. Swapping these roles for visual variety is prohibited.

rules.name: The Thai Line-Height Rule
rules.body: Body line-height is 1.6, always. Thai diacritics stack above and below base characters; anything below 1.5 clips them.

rules.name: The Fixed Scale Rule
rules.body: Do not use clamp() or viewport-relative font sizes. Fixed rem/px only. A heading that changes size as the window resizes creates instability in a data-heavy layout where column widths matter.

rules.name: The Flat-First Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are separated by tone, not by shadow. Add a shadow only when the element floats above the document flow. Ambient or decorative box-shadow on cards or table rows is prohibited.

dos: Do use the five semantic colors strictly by their role — role integrity is the system's trust signal.
Do separate surfaces tonally: #ffffff cards on #f0efe9 canvas. Depth through tone, not shadow.
Do use #241d3d for all <thead> rows — the dark header makes data tables authoritative and scannable.
Do use Sarabun at 1.6 line-height for all body text. Thai diacritics require it.
Do restrict the brand gradient to the login screen, active nav icon tile, and avatar.
Do use monospace (Courier New) for barcodes, product codes, document numbers, and weight values.
Do use the pill shape (100px radius) for status badges.
Do keep button shapes consistent at 8px radius across every screen.
donts: Don't use Action Indigo as a decorative accent. It signals 'press me' or 'you are here.'
Don't add ambient or decorative box-shadow to cards, stat tiles, or table rows. Shadow appears only on floating layers.
Don't introduce a new typeface. Sarabun handles every role.
Don't use clamp() or viewport-relative font sizes. Fixed scale only.
Don't put the brand gradient on interior buttons — login CTA and active nav icon tile only.
Don't make it look like a legacy ERP system, generic SaaS blue dashboard, budget POS app, or consumer social app.
Don't use motion choreography or page-load sequences. State-change transitions only, 130–250ms.
Don't use border-left > 1px as a colored stripe. Use background tints or full borders instead.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text). Emphasis is weight or size.
